# Perf

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Diagnostics` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class Perf
```

A tiny always-available profiler: named scopes, wall time, and managed allocation.

Off by default and free when off — [`Perf.Measure()`](Nfty.Core.Diagnostics.Perf.md#m-measure-system-string) returns a struct whose Dispose does nothing, so an unenabled scope costs one branch and no allocation. Turn it on with the `NFTY_PERF=1` environment variable, or from code with [`Perf.Enable()`](Nfty.Core.Diagnostics.Perf.md#m-enable), which is what the benchmark tests do.

Deliberately not BenchmarkDotNet: this measures whole user-facing operations inside the real app (opening a Set, realizing a row of thumbnails) rather than micro-benchmarking a method in isolation, and it has to be able to run in a GUI process. It is a stopwatch and a dictionary, which is the right size for the question.

Turns measurement on and clears whatever was collected before.

### Measure(string) { #m-measure-system-string }

```csharp
public static Perf.Scope Measure(string name);
```

Measures the enclosing block.

**Parameters**

- `name` (`string`) - The scope's name; totals accumulate per name.

**Returns.** A scope to dispose at the end of the block. Disposing a disabled scope does nothing.

**Example**

```csharp
using var _ = Perf.Measure("SetReader.Read");
```

### Report() { #m-report }

```csharp
public static string Report();
```

The snapshot as a fixed-width table.

**Returns.** One line per scope, plus a header. Empty string when nothing was measured.

**Remarks**

Formatted the way `Stats/`'s reports are — invariant, so two runs on two machines can be diffed.
